subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: The HPO Axis, Pulsatile GnRH, FSH and the LH Surge

steps.tx: The hormonal cascade from hypothalamus through pituitary to ovary governing reproduction is the **hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis**. Feedback loops at each level tune the cycle precisely. Disruption at any level produces amenorrhoea or irregular bleeding. Slow GnRH pulses favour FSH release, fast pulses favour LH, which is how one hormone steers two outputs.
steps.say: The HPO axis cascades from hypothalamus to ovary with feedback at each level.

steps.tx: Gonadotropin releasing hormone must arrive in pulses every hour or so to work, a rule of **pulsatile GnRH**. Continuous exposure paradoxically suppresses the pituitary, exploited by GnRH analogue drugs. Pulse frequency itself encodes FSH versus LH preference. GnRH analogues exploit this by first flaring, then shutting the pituitary down within two weeks.
steps.say: Pulsatile GnRH works hourly, while continuous exposure suppresses the pituitary.

steps.tx: The pituitary hormone recruiting the follicle cohort each cycle is **FSH**. Follicle stimulating hormone rises in the early follicular phase as inhibin and oestrogen fall. The follicle with most FSH receptors becomes dominant. The dominant follicle reaches 18 to 24 millimetres before rupture, growing about two millimetres a day.
steps.say: FSH recruits the follicle cohort, and the best receptor endowed follicle dominates.

steps.tx: Sustained high oestrogen switching feedback to positive triggers the midcycle **LH surge**. Luteinising hormone then resumes meiosis and ruptures the follicle within about thirty six hours. Urine kits detect this surge for fertility timing. Kits turn positive 12 to 36 hours before ovulation, timing intercourse for the fertile window.
steps.say: The LH surge follows sustained high oestrogen and ruptures the follicle in thirty six hours.

steps.tx: Negative feedback dominates most of the cycle, with oestrogen and inhibin restraining FSH, termed **feedback control**. Only the late follicular oestrogen peak flips the sign briefly. This single positive window times ovulation exactly. Inhibin B from the small cohort is the signal that trims FSH so only one follicle survives.
steps.say: Feedback control restrains FSH except for the brief positive window timing ovulation.

steps.tx: Kisspeptin neurons integrate metabolic and seasonal signals into GnRH pulses, acting as the **pulse generator**. Leptin deficiency from low weight silences them, explaining athletic amenorrhoea. Their discovery redefined axis physiology. Energy intake under about 30 kilocalories per kilogram of fat free mass silences the generator in athletes.
steps.say: Kisspeptin neurons generate GnRH pulses and fall silent with low leptin.

steps.tx: Prolactin suppresses GnRH pulsatility, linking breastfeeding and prolactinoma amenorrhoea by one **prolactin brake**. Dopamine tonically restrains prolactin, so stalk damage raises it. Restoring dopamine agonism restores cycles. Dopamine agonist treatment restores ovulation in most prolactinoma patients within weeks of prolactin normalising.
steps.say: The prolactin brake suppresses GnRH, linking lactation and prolactinoma amenorrhoea.

steps.tx: Thyroid and adrenal disorders disturb the axis secondarily, so screening them belongs to every cycle workup, called **axis screening**. TSH, prolactin and androgens are the minimum blood panel. Treating the gland often restores ovulation alone. Androgen excess points instead to polycystic ovaries or, when severe and fast, an androgen secreting tumour.
steps.say: Axis screening checks thyroid, prolactin and androgens in every cycle workup.

steps.tx: Ageing depletes follicles until inhibin falls and FSH climbs permanently at the **menopausal transition**. Cycles shorten then lengthen with anovulatory gaps. The same axis, starved of follicles, explains every perimenopausal symptom pattern. Hot flushes come from a narrowed thermoneutral zone as oestrogen falls, not from the high FSH itself.
steps.say: The menopausal transition climbs FSH permanently as follicles deplete.
